564_components.qod: Frame A, whose semantic kernel is A.eval(r)(f,x)=ATTRACT(f,x,r); its host is the recipient/goal r. The kernel agrees with the old qodaiin output, while its packaging as a Frame is new.
564_components.qok: Frame L, with L.eval(r)(f,x)=ALTER(f,x,r), alteration of the material with respect to the recipient part. This is a new frame value constrained only by the old qokar faculty meaning; it supplies neither complete assimilation nor a successful nourishment endpoint.
564_components.ar: The single generic function NOM:ProcessFrame→FacultySpec. NOM(F) retains F's process relation and named host role. It is never a RecipientRef, an assertion, or the acting faculty f.

564_application_rules: Forward case: a written Frame immediately followed by a written RecipientRef r yields F.eval(r). In qod|aiin this is the old attraction predicate awaiting f and x; the old separate goal argument must agree with r.

Backward case: a written Frame immediately followed by NOM yields NOM(F). The result's process relation and host role are inherited from that same Frame, not selected by the spelling of the whole word.

The backward rule is identical inside a licensed compound and across a real word boundary. A standalone ar therefore needs an immediately preceding complete written Frame expression; it cannot retrieve an unspoken frame or serve as a noun by itself.

Only the three compound cuts qod|aiin, qod|ar and qok|ar are licensed here. No arbitrary substring deletion, opposite-direction fallback, silent LOC_OWNER conversion or segmentation of every ar-ending word is licensed.
